 Keegan Murray (illness) did not practice on Saturday. 
 Murray returned to the starting lineup on Friday, but his status for Sunday’s game is now up in the air. Precious Achiuwa had been starting in his place, but he missed Friday’s game. If both end up missing Sunday’s game, Leaky Black would likely step into the starting unit.

 SAC 
 Forward 
 #13 
 The Kings will start Darius Acuff, Zach LaVine, DeAndre Hunter, Keegan Murray, and Domantas Sabonis on Friday against the Blazers. 
 Keegan Murray will re-enter the starting lineup and Precious Achiuwa will head to the bench. The change shouldn’t impact their value very much as Keegan played more minutes than Precious in last game.

 Precious Achiuwa (ankle) is out for Friday’s matchup with the Trail Blazers. 
 Achiuwa is dealing with left ankle soreness that will keep him sidelined for at least one game. With Achiuwa on the sideline, Keegan Murray could rejoin the starting five for the first time since returning from injury. 
 Precious Achiuwa 
 SAC 
 Forward 
 #9 
 Precious Achiuwa (leg) finished Tuesday’s loss to the Magic with 10 points (3-of-6 FGs, 3-of-3 FTs), three rebounds, one steal and one three-pointer. 
 Achiuwa had to leave Tuesday’s game with just under eight minutes left in the third quarter with a leg contusion and did not return. His early exit gave Dylan Cardwell (1/12/1/2/2) more playing time, and he logged 29 minutes off the bench. Keegan Murray (11/2/1 with four blocks and two three-pointers) played 24 minutes as he continues to work his way back from an ankle injury.

 Murray played 22 minutes off the bench in Sunday’s loss to the Heat, but took a hard fall in the second quarter, which potentially caused him to sprain his wrist. He’s been cleared to play against the Magic Tuesday and will likely take on his usual bench role.

 Keegan Murray (wrist) is questionable for Tuesday’s game against the Magic. 
 Murray took a hard fall during the second quarter of Sunday’s loss to the Heat. That may be why his right wrist is sore. Murray came off the bench in his first game back from an ankle injury. If he can’t play Tuesday, Daeqwon Plowden or Jonathan Mogbo may get more minutes. 
 Keegan Murray 
 SAC 
 Forward 
 #13 
 Keegan Murray (ankle) accounted for 10 points (3-of-10 FGs, 4-of-4 FTs), one rebound, two assists, two steals and one block in Sunday’s loss to the Heat. 
 Making his first appearance since October 23, Murray played a reserve role on Sunday. After playing stints of six, four and five minutes in the first three quarters, the Kings forward played the last 7:46 of the fourth quarter. Murray took a hard fall during the second quarter when he landed on his upper back after a Bobby Portis shot fake got him in the air, but he did not require any attention on the Kings’ bench. As Murray’s minutes increase, Precious Achiuwa (7/14/2/1 with one block) will likely see his minutes decrease after logging 36 minutes on Sunday.

 Darius Acuff Jr., Zach LaVine, De’Andre Hunter, Precious Achiuwa and Dylan Cardwell will start Sunday’s game against the Heat. 
 The Kings are without Domantas Sabonis (knee) for Sunday’s game, opening up a spot in the starting lineup. Cardwell will replace him, and the Kings will need his rebounding and defense. Also, Hunter reclaims his place in the lineup with Leaky Black heading to the bench. And Achiuwa remains in the starting lineup despite Keegan Murray returning from an ankle injury.

 Victor Wembanyama tallied 26 points (10-of-21 FGs, 2-of-3 FTs), 11 rebounds, six assists, one steal, five blocks and four three-pointers in Sunday’s win over the Jazz.

 Darius Garland amassed a game-high 27 points (10-of-18 FGs, 4-of-6 FTs), six rebounds, seven assists and one steal over 35 minutes to propel the Clippers to a 113-105 win over the Hornets on Sunday.
 Garland is clearly relishing his opportunity as the straw that stirs the drink during his Clippers debut, topping 20 points for the seventh time in 12 games this season. His lackluster supporting cast and minimal impact across most fantasy categories puts a clear lid on his ceiling, but he’s off to a nice start, averaging 21.3 points, 2.3 rebounds, 6.9 assists, 0.6 steals and 0.1 blocks. The Clippers have a busy three-game week ahead that features matchups against the Jazz, Spurs and Mavericks.
